minutes.headline: Planning Board leans toward minimal 'paper compliance' rezoning of Tritown to meet the state's MBTA housing mandate
minutes.summary: The board spent most of the meeting on the state-mandated MBTA Communities Act, hearing options from consultant Community Scale and leaning toward using the already-built Tritown (37 Young's Road) complex to satisfy the roughly 240-unit capacity requirement rather than upzoning new land, with public information sessions to follow. It also held public hearings on a scenic-road tree removal (approved) and a five-lot Towns and Harbor Road subdivision's storm water permit, sending the latter to paid peer review and continuing it to June 9, and voted to add a Finance Committee member to the Master Plan Steering Committee.

what_happened.line: Board leaned toward minimal 'paper compliance' rezoning, using the already-built Tritown complex to meet the state's MBTA housing mandate rather than adding new capacity elsewhere.
The board voted to require a peer-review deposit and continued the Towns and Harbor Road subdivision's storm water hearing to June 9.
The chair will schedule public information sessions on MBTA Communities zoning options, to be posted under the Open Meeting Law.
A scenic-road tree removal at 63 Lancaster Avenue was approved after the hearing closed.
The board added a Finance Committee member to the Master Plan Steering Committee.

why_it_matters: The MBTA Communities compliance choice determines whether new zoning capacity for housing is concentrated at one already-built site or spread to new land elsewhere in town.
The storm water peer review, funded by an applicant deposit, addresses residents' flooding and groundwater concerns near the proposed five-lot subdivision.
Planned public information sessions on MBTA Communities zoning are residents' chance to weigh in before any rezoning vote.
